newsitem.title: SPAIN: SWIMMING-KORNEYEV DISQUALIFIED AT EUROPEAN CHAMPS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-KORNEYEV DISQUALIFIED AT EUROPEAN CHAMPS.

text.p: Olympic bronze medallist Andrei Korneyev, involved in a doping furore at the Atlanta Games, was disqualified for a false start at the European swimming championships on Tuesday.

Korneyev's heat in the men's 100 metres breaststroke had already been held up by one false start before the Russian dived in ahead of the starting hooter on the second attempt to get the race underway.
That meant automatic disqualification for Korneyev and German Thomas Schmolt, who had caused the first false start and also took off too soon at the second attempt.

The two swimmers were ushered away again by the starter when they ignored the order for their dismissal and got back onto their starting blocks. Schmolt even scampered back once more before finally accepting the ruling.
Korneyev was initially stripped of his Olympic 200 breaststroke bronze medal when he tested positive for the stimulant bromantan but was reinstated on appeal.
The Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld the Russian appeal in Atlanta, ruling that too little was known about bromantan and the punishment too severe.
The Russian, 100 breaststroke bronze medallist at the 1995 European championships, will defend his European 200 breaststroke title on Friday.

Olympic champion Frederik DeBurghgraeve of Belgium, initially entered to defend his European 100 breaststroke crown, has been in indifferent form this year and decided in the end to stay away to concentrate on his preparations for next January's world championships in Perth, Australia.

Ireland's Michelle de Bruin, competing at a major meeting for the first time under her married name after winning three Olympic golds as Michelle Smith last year, qualified comfortably for the afternoon's 400 metres individual medley final.

De Bruin, swimming well within her powers, finished second in her heat behind Czech Hana Cerna and fourth overall in four minutes 48.75 seconds -- well outside the 4:39.18 with which she gained the first of her three golds at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics.
De Bruin, who won two golds and a silver at the 1995 European championships, is attempting to win an unprecedented five individual titles at this meeting.

It might have been seven but she had a late entry for the 100 butterfly turned down because she had missed the deadline and has pulled out of the 800 freestyle, whose final falls on the same day as her 200 butterfly title defence.
Ukraine's Yana Klochkova, who won the European junior title in Glasgow less than three weeks ago, sounded a challenge to De Bruin with the fastest qualifying time of 4:47.52.
Olympic silver medallist Sandra Voelker led qualifiers in the women's 100 metres freestyle in 55.46 seconds.
Fellow German Jens Kruppa, bronze medallist in April's world short-course championships, showed the way in the men's breaststroke (1:02.38).
Italy's Massimiliano Rosolino topped men's 200 freestyle qualifiers in 1:49.19, with Britons James Salter (1:49.50) and Paul Palmer (1:49.98) second and third overall.
